headline: Bone age
body: It's five axes pulling on the same clock at once.
punch: Which is why single hormone thinking keeps getting predictions wrong.

headline: Most explanations
body: It's estrogen. It's growth hormone. It's thyroid. Each one is describing a single input to a system with several, then generalising from it.
punch: Clinical reviews don't get that luxury.

headline: The full set starts
body: Growth hormone and IGF-1 drive proliferation and the growth velocity you actually see. They move height fast and bone age comparatively slowly.
punch: This is the axis that buys you time.

headline: Then thyroid hormone
body: Thyroid hormone is required for normal chondrocyte maturation. Too little and maturation stalls. Too much and the whole schedule speeds up.
punch: Thyroid is the tempo, not the volume.

headline: Estrogens
body: Estrogen is the dominant driver of skeletal maturation and eventual fusion, and androgens contribute a lot by getting converted into it.
punch: This is the axis that spends your remaining time.

headline: Androgens
body: They raise growth velocity and accelerate skeletal maturation at the same time. You get taller faster while having less time left to do it in.
punch: Two effects pulling opposite ways from one hormone.

headline: Which is why
body: Your age tells you how long you've existed. Bone age tells you how much growth capacity you have left, and only one of those can be changed.

headline: And why the tradeoff
body: Anything that speeds up growth velocity through the androgen axis also spends skeletal maturation. Optimising one number while ignoring the other is how people end up shorter.
punch: Growing faster and growing longer are competing goals.
